title: Failover: ingest region health signals (synthetics + metrics) into aggregator w/ validation + defaults
author: Caleb Johnson
release_notes: Internal-only: region health aggregator now consumes synthetic probe results and canonical metrics-based signals with config validation + sane defaults. No customer-facing API change.
body:
Summary: This PR wires region health signal ingestion into the region-health-aggregator so the trigger engine/orchestrator can consume a single normalized, validated stream of health indicators per region. We ingest (1) synthetic probe events (edge-to-region and region-to-upstream probes) and (2) metrics-derived health signals (5xx/error ratio, tail latency, saturation/queue depth, dependency health) from Telemetry. The main deliverables here are ingestion adapters + a canonical schema, plus strict config validation and defaults to avoid "silent" gaps.

Context / why: Recent incidents showed we were debating failover with incomplete/late signals and inconsistent thresholds between dashboards and automation (see SUP-19240 and SUP-19312 symptoms). ENG-2842 defines the signal contract; ENG-2843 is the aggregator implementation. This PR focuses specifically on getting real inputs flowing in, with guardrails so misconfigured regions/environments fail fast.

What changed (high level):
- Added a new ingestion pipeline in region-health-aggregator:
  - Synthetic probes: consumes `synthetics.probe_result.v1` events (success, latency_ms, packet_loss_pct, source_region, target_region, route) and maps them into normalized per-region indicators.
  - Metrics signals: pulls from Telemetry query endpoints for canonical timeseries (error_rate, p95_latency_ms, p99_latency_ms, gpu_util, queue_depth, batcher_backlog, upstream_dependency_error_rate).
- Introduced `RegionHealthSignalConfig` with validation:
  - Validates region names, required signal presence, allowed windows, and sane threshold ranges.
  - Enforces minimum coverage: each region must have at least one synthetic network probe and the core metrics set (error + latency) unless explicitly marked as `signal_profile=limited` (e.g., some Private environments).
  - Rejects configs that would cause flappy updates (e.g., windows < 30s, or mismatched scrape intervals).
- Added defaults:
  - Default windows and aggregation intervals (60s window, 10s publish cadence) unless overridden.
  - Default mappings for known regions (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1) and envs (staging/prod).
  - Default "unknown" handling: missing signal data sets indicator state=UNKNOWN w/ reason instead of implicitly healthy.
- Normalization + persistence:
  - Normalizes all inputs into `RegionHealthSnapshot` (per region, per indicator) and persists with TTL for the trigger engine.
  - Adds `source` and `freshness_ms` fields used by later safety checks/hysteresis.
- Observability:
  - Emits `region_health_ingestion_lag_ms`, `region_health_signal_missing_total`, `region_health_snapshot_publish_total`, and per-signal parse/validation errors.
  - Adds structured logs on config rejection with actionable messages.

Config details:
- New config file: `config/region_health_signals.yaml`
- Example (illustrative):
  - `signals.core.error_rate.metric = gateway.request_errors / gateway.requests`
  - `signals.core.p99_latency.metric = gateway.request_latency_ms{quantile="0.99"}`
  - `signals.network.packet_loss.synthetic_route = edge->region`
- Validation fails startup if required keys are missing, unless `ALLOW_PARTIAL_SIGNAL_COVERAGE=true` is set (intended only for dev).

Testing:
- Unit tests for schema validation + defaulting behavior.
- Integration test using a stub Telemetry server and a replayed synthetic probe fixture.
- Added a "no data" test verifying we publish UNKNOWN with reasons and do not mark the region healthy.

Rollout plan:
- Ship behind existing aggregator deployment (no flag needed; behavior is additive).
- Staging first: verify synthetic and metrics inputs present for all staging regions.
- Production next: enable for the three primary hosted regions; Private environments can opt-in via installer config (follow-up PR).

Follow-ups / not in this PR:
- Wiring this snapshot output into the trigger evaluation engine thresholds/hysteresis (ENG-2844).
- Safe-to-failover gating based on dependency health and capacity (ENG-2845).
- Dashboard work is tracked in ENG-2847; this PR only adds emitter metrics.

Risk notes:
- Strict validation is intentionally opinionated; we chose fail-fast because partially wired automation is worse than none. There is an escape hatch for dev but not for prod.
- Missing data defaults to UNKNOWN (not healthy) to prevent accidental "green" regions when ingestion is broken.

Screenshots/links:
- N/A (service-side only). For local testing, see `./region-health-aggregator --print-effective-config`.

Checklist:
- [x] Added tests
- [x] Added metrics for ingestion errors/lag
- [x] Updated runbook snippet for "signal missing" troubleshooting
- [x] Verified backward compatibility with existing aggregator consumers
commits: region-health-aggregator: add synthetic probe consumer + normalizer
telemetry: add canonical metric query client + retries/timeouts
config: add RegionHealthSignalConfig schema + strict validation
tests: add config validation cases + telemetry stub integration test
obs: add ingestion lag/missing-signal metrics + structured logs
review_conversation: Allison Grant: Can we ensure missing signal data never shows up as healthy? We had a case where the dashboard looked green because the query returned empty.

Caleb Johnson (author): Yep — this PR defaults missing/empty to UNKNOWN and records `reason=NO_DATA` plus `freshness_ms`. Consumers can treat UNKNOWN as not-healthy. Added a test: `publishes_unknown_on_empty_timeseries`.
Emily Zhao: Synthetic probes: how do we avoid false positives when an edge POP is impaired but region is fine? Also which routes are mandatory?

Caleb Johnson (author): We require >=2 probe sources per region in prod (config validation enforces it). Snapshot stores per-source outcomes; later trigger logic will use majority/median. For now ingestion just normalizes + publishes; routing on majority is follow-up in ENG-2844.
Jordan Lee: Telemetry client retry policy looks aggressive (5 retries). Any chance this adds load during incidents?

Caleb Johnson (author): Good catch. Reduced to 2 retries with capped backoff and added `timeout=750ms` per query. Also added a circuit-breaker metric; if telemetry is failing, we publish UNKNOWN instead of hammering it.
Miles Thornton: I like fail-fast validation but worried about prod deploys failing if a single region config is off. Can we scope validation per env/region?

Caleb Johnson (author): Validation is per-environment config bundle. In prod, we only include prod regions; staging includes staging regions. Also added `--print-effective-config` to make reviews easier. We can add a "warn-only" mode later if needed, but current stance is fail-fast.
Aisha Bello: Please ensure indicators/windows are aligned with burn-rate alert windows (multi-window). At least document recommended minimums.
Caleb Johnson (author): Added comments in `config/region_health_signals.yaml` and a guard that rejects windows < 30s. We’re using 60s default which maps cleanly to the shortest burn window.
Miles Thornton: Approving with the retry change + added documentation.
Allison Grant: Approved. Thanks for the UNKNOWN behavior.
